artifacts.summary: Phase 2 (sapience-remember.sh Project Tagging and Its First Test Suite) completed and committed; resume point and context for Phase 3.

completion_data.completion_summary: Added optional runtime project-key resolution, a --project-key override flag, and the degrade-on-failure rule (never a refusal) to sapience-remember.sh, plus its first regression suite (test-sapience-remember.sh, 11 assertions across 7 cases including the two Ruling 1/3 policy invariants). Registered the new suite in manifest.json via sync-manifest-scripts.sh --write and confirmed suite_selection_select now resolves it for sapience-remember.sh. Unlinked-case output confirmed byte-identical to the pre-change script; scoped verify-touched.sh battery green aside from one pre-existing EXPECTED-flaky timeout; no Rule Q finding.

memory_candidates.content: sync-manifest-scripts.sh derives each extension's on-disk script set from `git ls-files <ext>/scripts`, not a plain filesystem walk. A brand-new, not-yet-`git add`-ed test file is therefore invisible to it (reports as already in sync even though the file exists on disk) until it is staged. The fix is `git add` the new file before running `sync-manifest-scripts.sh --write`.

suite_selection_select's resolution for a given script relies on a grep-based reference stratum over the DEPLOYED .claude/scripts/tests/ tree, not the source store. A brand-new test suite that references its subject script by name will not appear in suite_selection_select's output until a redeploy has copied it into the deployed tree -- confirms the existing memory note about agent-definition-file NO-SUITE-BY-CLASS probes generalizes to this case too.

A fixed-content test subject with no standalone deployed copy (e.g. an extension's settings-fragment.json, which is merge-targeted into .claude/settings.local.json rather than copied verbatim) must be resolved via common_test_ext_root(REPO_ROOT) + '<ext-name>/<file>', never a SCRIPT_DIR-relative '../../file' path -- the relative path only works when the suite itself happens to run from the source tree, and silently breaks when the same suite runs from a deployed .claude/scripts/tests/ copy (a different directory depth with no sibling settings-fragment.json at all).

sapience_notes.subject: sapience-remember.sh project-key resolution degrade rule
sapience_notes.value: sapience-remember.sh's new project-key resolution (added in the sapience_linked_repo_write_and_capture_policy task) deliberately degrades to an untagged write with a stderr warning on every resolution failure (no binding, non-JSON GET response, no matching cid, matching entry with no key), never refusing -- the opposite of sapience-publish.sh ko's refuse-on-failure behavior. Rationale: sapience-remember.sh serves a non-interactive, bounded postflight note set where losing a note outright is worse than writing it untagged.

sapience_notes.subject: sapience-publish.sh ko's project-key resolution shape reused verbatim
sapience_notes.value: sapience-remember.sh's project-key resolution (binding cid -> GET /v1/people/projects -> jq-matched key, never project_cid) is a direct copy of sapience-publish.sh ko's existing runtime-resolution block and defensive response-unwrapping, confirming that shape is now established precedent across both Sapience write scripts rather than a one-off.

sapience_notes.subject: sync-manifest-scripts.sh's git-ls-files dependency
sapience_notes.value: sync-manifest-scripts.sh's 'on disk' script count for an extension is derived from `git ls-files <ext>/scripts`, not a filesystem walk -- a newly-created, not-yet-staged test file is invisible to it until `git add`-ed. Measured live: the script reported sapience as fully in sync (20/20) immediately after a new test file was written to disk, and only detected it (21/21 after --write) once the file was staged.

sapience_notes.subject: suite_selection_select's deployed-tree dependency for a new suite
sapience_notes.value: suite_selection_select's grep-based reference stratum resolves a new test suite for its subject script only after that suite has been copied into the deployed .claude/scripts/tests/ tree -- a suite that exists only in the source store (agent-system/extensions/<ext>/scripts/tests/) is invisible to it until a redeploy. Measured live this session: the lookup returned the suite only after `deploy-headless.sh` ran a second time following the suite's creation and manifest registration.

sapience_notes.subject: Write-tool-created shell scripts lack the executable bit
sapience_notes.value: A new .sh test file created via the Write tool does not carry the executable bit; run-all.sh's deployed-tree discovery reports it as [SKIP] not executable (exec-bit regression?) until chmod +x is applied at the SOURCE-STORE copy and the tree is redeployed (chmod on only the deployed copy would be discarded on the next redeploy, per the source-store/deploy-boundary rule).
